scenario.label: Engagement Director, first 90 days
scenario.brief: We hired an Engagement Director to own the relationships with our five largest clients and to take those conversations off me within ninety days. I need to know whether he understands the role the way I described it, whether he is taking ownership or waiting to be told, whether what he says he will do actually happens, whether his blockers are real, and whether by day ninety I can stop being in those meetings. If the answer is no I need to know whether the problem is him, the brief, or the onboarding.
scenario.theDecision: He understood the role as account management and reporting; she meant owning the commercial relationship and the renewal conversation. Neither of them has noticed the difference. He is competent and diligent inside his own reading of the job, delivers everything he commits to, and is not becoming autonomous because nobody has told him autonomy is the point. A right answer says the gap is in the brief rather than in the person, and names the sentence where the two readings first diverge.

people.name: Dr Amina Bello
people.remit: Chief executive. Hired him and wants out of the client meetings by day ninety.
people.truth: She wants him owning the commercial relationship: pricing conversations, renewals, and the decision about which clients to keep. people.name: Tobi Adewale
people.remit: Engagement Director. Owns the relationships with the five largest clients.
people.truth: He understood the job as account management: keep the clients happy, report on health, escalate problems. He has never discussed price or renewal with anybody because he does not believe that is his to do. He has attended every meeting with Amina and assumed she wanted to lead them. He delivers everything he says he will.
people.manner: Diligent and precise about what he has done. Says yes to things and does them. Does not volunteer a view about the shape of his own job unless asked directly.
